claims.content: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory products by applying filters and combinable search criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory products by applying filters and combinable search criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer uses the product browse/search capability, applies one or more available filters or search criteria, and the system displays the filtered product list matching those criteria.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is in the auction inventory product browsing/search context and starts the browse/search action.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The system displays a filtered product list matching the Customer's selected browse/search criteria.
in_scope_actions: Apply and combine filters or search parameters
excluded_adjacent_actions: Downstream auction administration or product management

claims.content: Customer
The Auction Admin Main Menu is open and has automatically populated the Today's Auction Inventory Recap Section with key inventory data.

The Customer starts the browse/search action by entering a Product ID (e.g., ABC123) or Customer Email Address and clicking the 'Go' button, or by selecting search parameters such as Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range and then clicking 'Find Product'.
The Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the auction inventory.

The Customer applies one or more combinable browse/search criteria, such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone Type, Material Type, Material Purity, Brand, Product ID, Cost Range, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Customer Email Address. Multiple scrolling list-box filters can be selected simultaneously using the Control key; Product ID searches may use wildcards (* or %), and Cost Range may be entered as low and high values.
The Customer submits the search by clicking the 'Go' button or the 'Find Product' button.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment.
The result rows show the matching auction items, each with thumbnail images, bid values, start/end times, duration, and increment amount.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of starting with Endeca browse/search navigation, the Customer may access the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists Categories, Product Types, and Gemstone Types as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages, or via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types or product types that contain direct links to relevant product categories.

Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may choose to scope the search by selecting 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory' via radio buttons; this selection does not impact the results of the 'Red status' columns.
Diverges from Step 2: The Customer may also use radio buttons to view items with or without images, and with or without a valid (sellable) location.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may switch between List View and Catalog View display modes for the product results.

Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may group the results using a scrolling list box (e.g., by Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Brand, Inventory Realm, or Ring Size), and the system generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 4: If the search returns no matches, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page instead of the 'Search Results' table. The page includes (1) an apology message stating no matches were found, (2) a 'Search Tips' section with five suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support), and (3) a 'May We Suggest' section containing static popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data. Exit: the exception branch terminates with the 'No Results Found' page displayed.
Diverges from Main Flow Step 1: If the Customer clicks on a link that contains no product (this will happen for collectibles routinely), the system serves a 'no results found' page.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 4: Before displaying Search Results, the system prevents any product without an available image from appearing on search results, catalog pages, or product details pages; matching items lacking images are therefore excluded from the result set.

missing_aspects: Recovery/return navigation from the 'No Results Found' page back into search or browse is not documented.
The explicit display behavior when the no-image pre-filter removes all matching items (e.g., whether an empty Search Results table or the 'No Results Found' page is shown) is undocumented.
Outcome when all matching items lack images (empty result set vs other behavior)
Explicit return to Main Flow Step 4

claims.content: The system displays a filtered product list matching the Customer's applied browse/search criteria. When the results are shown in catalog/product-module view, each item is represented by a Product Module containing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.

When the results are shown in list view, the system displays a table titled 'Search Results' with columns for Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #, linked to the SKU History page), Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment; the rows show the matching auction items with thumbnail images, bid values, start/end times, duration, and increment amount.

When the Customer's successful search is by Product ID, the system displays a 'Search Results for Item' section with a table containing Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder, populated with rows for the matching auction history.
